items.stem: A newly appointed CEO is spending most of each week in operational reviews. What is the strongest argument that this is a strategic problem?

options.text: The CEO's unique contribution is direction-setting and capital allocation, which operational immersion crowds out
options.rationale: Correct: only the CEO can set enterprise direction and allocate capital, so that work must not be crowded out.

options.text: Operational reviews are never useful for a CEO
options.rationale: Too absolute; some operational insight is valuable.

options.text: CEOs should delegate all decisions to the top team
options.rationale: Direction and capital decisions cannot be fully delegated.

options.text: The board prefers CEOs who avoid operations
options.rationale: Board preference is not the underlying reason.

items.explanation: Correct: only the CEO can set enterprise direction and allocate capital, so that work must not be crowded out.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO actions most directly express the CEO's capital-allocation responsibility? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Shifting investment from a declining unit to a priority growth business
options.rationale: Correct: reallocating capital toward priorities is core CEO work.

options.text: Deciding to divest a non-core business unit
options.rationale: Correct: divestiture reallocates capital out of a non-core business.
This is an operational purchasing decision, not capital allocation.

options.text: Editing the wording of a press release
options.rationale: Communications editing is not capital allocation.
Scheduling is administrative, not capital allocation.

items.explanation: Correct: reallocating capital toward priorities is core CEO work.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A CEO announces a clear three-priority strategy but a year later nothing has changed. What is the most likely strategic cause rather than an execution excuse?

options.text: Budgets, headcount and incentives were never realigned to the three priorities
options.rationale: Correct: strategy that is not reflected in resource allocation does not change behaviour.

options.text: The priorities were communicated only once
options.rationale: Repetition helps but is secondary to resource realignment.

options.text: The market moved faster than expected
options.rationale: Possible but not the most likely internal cause.

items.explanation: Correct: strategy that is not reflected in resource allocation does not change behaviour.
